posts.title: Introduction
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

The Developer Console is the design system Namaste Salesforce is built from. It borrows its visual language from developer tools — mono indices, code-comment labels, hairline borders, terminal-row lists — because Apex is Salesforce's own language and this site teaches people to write it.

The five rules

  1. The hairline is the structure, not the shadow. One 1px border draws everything; shadows are near-flat. Elevation = the border brightens to brand blue on hover — nothing floats, nothing lifts.
  2. Monospace is a structural material. Fira Code renders every index, duration, timestamp, status tag and section label. Inter is reserved for prose and headings. This is what makes a list of lessons read as data and a paragraph read as writing, without touching color.
  3. One signal color. Brand blue #0176D3 is the only color that means "interactive" or "active". Status shows as a small dot + mono text, never a background wash.
  4. Sharp, specific geometry. Cards 6px, buttons and inputs 4px. Pills are reserved for true pills: tags and segmented controls.
  5. Motion is instant. 120–180ms plain ease-out. No spring, no bounce, no hover-lift. The one exception is the gentle float loop on decorative illustrations.

Three layers

LayerFolderContains
0 · Foundationassets/css/0-foundation/Tokens, variables and mixins only — colors, type scales, spacing, borders, elevation, motion, backgrounds. No selectors that paint UI.
1 · Elementsassets/css/1-elements/Bare HTML — headings, links, lists, blockquotes, tables, code — styled by the foundation. Everything you see in these docs' own body text.
2 · Componentsassets/css/2-components/The UI library — buttons, badges, inputs, cards, curriculum, navbar, code window.

How to use it

Build markup with Tailwind utilities on the token set (bg-surface, text-ink, rounded-card, shadow-card) and reach for ns-* component classes when a pattern already exists. Never hard-code a color, radius or shadow — if a value doesn't exist as a token, add it to the foundation first. Toggle the site theme while reading: every specimen in this section re-renders in the navy console dark mode.

posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

Two typefaces, two jobs, defined in 0-foundation/typography.css and self-hosted as variable fonts (0-foundation/fonts.css).

Inter — the prose material

Display
Heading 1 — 2.25rem
Heading 2 — 1.75rem
Heading 3 — 1.375rem
Heading 4 — 1.125rem

Body 1rem / 1.65 — comfortable reading measure, max 45rem.

Small 0.875rem — captions and meta lines.

Fira Code — the data material

Label — 01 · 12 lessons · 4h 30m code => != :: ligatures Kicker — a code comment

Every index, duration, timestamp, status tag and section label uses the mono/label scale: --size-label 0.6875rem, uppercase, tracked --tracking-label 0.09em, weight 700, ink --color-label.

Rules

  • Headings are Inter 800; body is Inter 400. Nothing between except 600/700 for UI emphasis.
  • If it's a number, a duration, an index or a label — it's Fira Code, tabular, uppercase.
  • Sentence case everywhere. The only all-caps text is the mono label scale.

Defined in 0-foundation/borders.css. The 1px hairline (--color-border) is the system's structuring device — cards, inputs, rows and tags are all drawn with it.

Radii

Rules

  • Nothing is rounded just because rounding is a default — 6px cards, 4px controls, pills for tags.
  • Hover brightens the hairline to brand-500; it never adds a shadow.
  • Use the ns-hairline mixin (inset ring) when a border must not change the box size.

posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

Defined in 0-foundation/motion.css. State changes resolve like a console: fast and literal.

Tokens

TokenValueUse
--duration-fast120mshover, press, focus

--ease-outcubic-bezier(.2,.6,.2,1)the house curve — also Tailwind's ease-out

animate-fade-up

Rules

  • Hover = border brightens + an accent line. Press = instant opacity dim. Never translateY, never scale-pop.
  • The float loop (animate-float) is for decorative illustrations only.
  • Everything respects prefers-reduced-motion — animation collapses to instant.

Everything on this page is bare HTML — no classes. The element layer (1-elements/typography.css) styles it wherever content renders.

A second-level heading

Body text at 1rem/1.65 with a 45rem measure. Here is an unstyled link — brand ink with a soft underline that sharpens on hover — plus bold emphasis, italics, and inline SELECT Id FROM Account.

A third-level heading

Keyboard input renders as keys: press ⌘ K to open search. Highlighted text uses mark. Small print looks like this: fine print at 0.875rem.

A fourth-level heading

Headings balance their line wraps (text-wrap: balance) and anchored headings scroll clear of the sticky header automatically.

posts.title: Element — Lists
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

Lists are data-adjacent, so their markers borrow the system's materials: brand dots for unordered, mono tabular numbers for ordered.

Unordered

  • Brand-blue disc markers
  • Comfortable 0.3rem rhythm between items
  • Nesting keeps the same voice
    • second level
    • still quiet

Ordered

  1. Numbers render in Fira Code, tabular
  2. So multi-digit lists align perfectly
  3. Reads as a sequence, not a sentence

Task-style content

For checklists inside lessons, prefer a plain ordered list with a clear verb per item — the platform does not use decorative checkboxes in prose.
